subject: Reading model summaries while using auxiliary variables

messages.author: 5d9ca4aba820f1f5
messages.subject: Reading model summaries while using auxiliary variables
parts:
Hey,

thanks for making MplusAutomation, I had to switch from lavaan for some yet unimplemented features and I'm really glad
I could keep some of my workflow.

I have a small problem, because MplusAutomation doesn't yet know how to deal with auxiliary variables:

#Error in extractValue(pattern = thisField$regexPattern, sectionText, filename,  : 
#  More than one match found for parameter: Number of Free Parameters
#  model1.out

so it gets confused by the below part.

Number of Free Parameters                      72

Loglikelihood Including the Auxiliary Part

          H0 Value                      -33644.020
          H0 Scaling Correction Factor      1.7239
            for MLR
          H1 Value                      -33540.976
          H1 Scaling Correction Factor      1.4931
            for MLR

Information Criteria Including the Auxiliary Part

          Number of Free Parameters            105
          Akaike (AIC)                   67498.040
          Bayesian (BIC)                 68080.639
          Sample-Size Adjusted BIC       67747.054
            (n* = (n + 2) / 24)


I'd gladly add the relevant code myself, I just downloaded the package source. 
Have you considered using Github for development to make it easier for others 
to contribute?

Best,

Ruben

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Reading model summaries while using auxiliary variables
parts:
Hi Ruben,

Thanks for the note. I am glad that MplusAutomation is useful to you
and appreciate the offer to add relevant code. I will look into what
needs to change to address auxiliary variables properly (or Michael
may if he beats me to it---he can be awfully fast).

As Michael is the primary author, I think it is up to him the platform
to develop the package. One nice feature of R forge is it does
automated builds. That said, if you are interested in contributing, I
am open to thinking about mirroring the R forge repository on github.
You could then fork that branch, make changes, send me a pull request,
and then I would check the code and merge it back with the R forge
repository. I already use git svn, so I do not think it would be that
much extra work on my part.

The other area where contributions could be nice is creating more
examples---if I did mirror R forge on github, a Wiki page and some
FAQs could be useful supplements to the great vignette. I like the
idea of users being able to share sample output files and contribute
little examples of using the package/linking R and Mplus.

Just thinking out loud really---would be nice to hear from any other
users on this too. There is not much point to switching the current
development process if no one else is going to contribute.

Cheers,

Josh

messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Reading model summaries while using auxiliary variables
parts:
Hi Ruben,

I like Github and use it for other projects, so I'm happy to move things in this direction. I think it makes it easier for others to contribute, which is certainly welcome  Also, with the devtools package, it's pretty easy to install dev versions from Github into R, so the auto-build on R-forge is potentially less of an advantage than it used to be. Anyway, Josh and I will talk more offline about the development process, but given your eagerness to help with some features that would be useful to all (R-squared) , let's move ahead with Github.

Here's the repo:

https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation

We look forward to your contributions. Speaking of, do you want me to look at the auxiliary issue, or are you already working on this? As you said, the challenge with the package is that every Mplus output can lead to exceptions in the logic of the parser, so if we haven't seen a certain output before, the parser may not know what to do. I am happy to look at the Aux issue, or for you to take it on.

Best wishes,
Michael
